themes.summary: G7 ordered release of 100 million barrels by February and US DOE offered 40 million barrels of sour SPR crude, pressing prices and differentials lower, though analysts call it a short-term fix.
Hormuz transits fell to 11 on Oct. 1 after a tanker was struck, with VLCC freight around $230/mt and Dated Brent far above Dubai.
US diesel export ban threat and Chinese product export halt lifted cracks, then G7 release cut them back; ULSD crack versus WTI settled at $97.94/b.
Ukrainian strikes hit Volgograd and Samara, almost half of Russian refining was offline by end-August, and Urals flows shifted from India to China.

themes.theme: Sour crude weakness as Middle East supply returns
themes.summary: Johan Sverdrup fell more than $10/b in four sessions and Middle East flows to India rose to 82.7 million barrels, though Gulf cash Dubai/Murban/Oman premiums rose on Oct. 2.
Suezmax Guyana-UKC hit w1,000 and VLCC Gulf-China sits near record, discouraging Chinese crude purchases and cutting runs.
Chinese refiners are cutting throughput as freight above $5/b breaks margins, with state utilization at 76.4% in September and further cuts expected in November.
